headline: Revenue ramps but a one-time charge widens the loss
summary_short: AST SpaceMobile's Q2 2026 revenue rose to $31.5 million from $1.2 million a year ago, but a $125.9 million one-time loss on involuntary conversion widened the net loss to $230.9 million.
summary_long: Revenue of $31.5M was driven by gateway deliveries and U.S. Government milestones met, off a near-zero year-ago base ($1.2M). Total operating expenses jumped to $329.1M, up $165.0M q/q, primarily from a $125.9M loss on involuntary conversion plus higher G&A ($20.3M), cost of revenues ($11.9M), and engineering costs ($3.2M). Net loss attributable to common stockholders widened to $230.9M ($0.77/share). The company had $2,288.3M of cash and cash equivalents (down from $3,029.6M q/q) after $859.2M of six-month capex and a $100M capital advance to Ligado, partly offset by $1,060.6M of debt proceeds; a July 2026 convertible-notes raise added $1.15B more. Revenue backlog reached ~$1.30B, and management reaffirmed FY2026 revenue guidance of $150-$200M.
confidence_notes: The y/y revenue and expense percentage changes are inflated by a near-zero prior-year base (AST SpaceMobile was pre-revenue-scale a year ago) — treat the multiples as directional, not precisely comparable growth rates. The $125.9M 'loss on involuntary conversion' is a one-time charge, likely satellite-related; the filing separately discloses $21.6M of insurance proceeds received from the BB7 launch in the same period, which may be a related but distinct recovery.

drivers.explanation: Growth was driven by gateway deliveries and U.S. Government milestones met, consistent with the company's plan for a quarterly revenue ramp during 2026.
The $165.0M sequential increase was primarily a $125.9M loss on involuntary conversion, plus higher G&A, cost of revenues, and engineering services costs.
Decline reflects $859.2M of six-month capex and a $100M capital advance to Ligado, partly offset by $1,060.6M of debt proceeds during the same period.
Management pointed to 60+ signed MNO partnerships covering 3 billion-plus subscribers, a ~$1.30B revenue backlog, and a fortified balance sheet as it prepares for 2026 beta service.
